historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (-2.4%) diverges from EPS 5yr CAGR (-10.4%) by more than 30%: book value is held flat by the ~100% payout policy, so equity growth says nothing about earnings power. Base-case growth is anchored on management's FY2027 'revenue expected to grow' guidance and long-run 1.5-2% nominal, not on the equity CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: All series measured FY2026 vs FY2023 (3yr) and FY2021 (5yr, the COVID-toy peak). Owner-FCF CAGRs are on reported FCF less SBC and interest income; they are only slightly below reported because SBC is ~0.2% of revenue -- the collapse is working capital (FY2026 +US$79m build) and a high FY2021 base, not SBC.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 delivers the guided revenue recovery (+4%) as ELP standalone launches, LeapMove expansion and Toy Story 5 / licensed lines rebuild North American sell-in after the April-2025 tariff shipment halt, and new LTE/Gigaset devices lift TEL, while CMS holds flat. Gross margin dips on AI-driven component inflation, so EBITDA margin troughs near 10.9% before recovering to the ~11.5% mid-cycle as Muar and Tecate absorb tariff-exposed US volume. Beyond FY2029 growth fades to 1.5%: shrinking birth cohorts and the residential-phone decline are offset, not overcome, by EMS diversification. VTech remains a debt-free ~100%-payout cash cow growing roughly with inflation.
scenario_narratives.bull: Tariffs stabilise and the China+1 footprint becomes a selling point: Malaysia's doubled capacity and Mexico win US EMS customers fleeing China (Wi-Fi routers, IoT, professional audio), CMS grows mid-single digits, LeapMove becomes a platform franchise and the AI baby monitor rolls out globally. Material costs normalise and the two-year gross-margin expansion (28.2% FY2022 -> 32.7% FY2026) resumes, taking EBITDA margin back toward 12.8% -- still below the FY2020-21 COVID peak of 13-14%. Revenue compounds ~3.5% for five years and 2% thereafter.
scenario_narratives.bear: US-China tariffs escalate again and repeat FY2026's multi-week North American shipment halt; retailers push order timing and demand price concessions, ELP shrinks with birth rates, cordless-phone decline accelerates, and a CMS customer program ends without replacement. Revenue falls ~7% over four years then flat-lines, and with component costs elevated and fixed-cost deleverage EBITDA margin settles near 9.5% (below the FY2023 trough of 10.7%). The balance sheet stays debt-free, so this is a lower dividend, not a solvency case; working-capital release on a shrinking top line partly cushions cash flow.

valuation_philosophy.summary: VTech is valued as a mature, debt-free, near-100%-payout manufacturer: a USD owner-FCF stream with leases charged in the flows, risk carried in a bear-weighted scenario set rather than the discount rate, and a 12x terminal cap reflecting a slow-growing, cyclical consumer-electronics business. The question the price answers is not growth but durability of an ~11% EBITDA margin through tariff shocks and secular category decline.
key_risks_to_valuation: US tariff escalation on China-made goods (FY2026 precedent: multi-week US shipment halt, NA ELP -25% in H1)
Structural decline in the core customer base (birth rates) and in residential phones
Component-cost inflation from AI-driven shortages compressing gross margin in FY2027
Working-capital absorption: inventory days at a five-year high (128); cash conversion has been volatile (FY2026 OCF -45%)
CMS customer concentration -- single programs ending (hearables, washing-machine PCBA) move segment results
~US$18m of cash sits in PRC banks under FX-control rules; H1 seasonal cash troughs mean not all year-end cash is truly excess

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (0303.HK) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range HK$47.80-67.90. FX from Yahoo USDHKD=X, parity vs OTC ADR VTKLY.
data_sources.financials: VTech Holdings Annual Reports FY2019-FY2026 and Interim Reports H1 FY2025-H1 FY2026 (research/0303.HK/Extracted), via research/0303.HK/Reports/0303.HK_Metrics.csv and the kpis table; balance sheet and cash flow lines from AR FY2026 pp.116-120.
data_sources.qualitative: research/0303.HK/Reports/0303.HK_Analysis.json (FY2027 outlook from the 21 May 2026 annual results).

inputs.share_count_basis: Diluted weighted-average ordinary shares FY2026 (AR FY2026 EPS note, line 7214: 253.3m, after adjusting for shares held for the Share Award Scheme). Held FLAT: SBC (Share Award + Share Option schemes, US$4.1m) is expensed in the flows; the Share Award Scheme is funded by on-market purchases (US$3.4m FY2026), option exercises add ~0.1-0.2%/yr which the SBC charge covers.
inputs.sbc_source: AR FY2026 cash flow statement lines 6186-6187: Share Award Scheme 3.8 + Share Option Scheme 0.3 = US$4.1m. No net-share-settlement tax withholding (EquityAwardTaxes = 0); awards are satisfied from shares bought on market by the scheme trustee.
inputs.fx_note: Statements are in US$ (AR FY2026 'US$ million' throughout); HKEX quote is HKD. Model -> quote rate USD/HKD 7.8472 (Yahoo USDHKD=X, 2026-10-09, inside the 7.75-7.85 HKMA peg band). Parity check: HK$52.00 / 7.8472 = US$6.63 vs OTC ADR VTKLY (1 ADR = 1 share) US$6.87 at 2026-10-08 close -- a 3.6% gap, consistent with an illiquid, one-day-staler OTC print rather than a direction error (the wrong direction would be off by ~60x).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T08:08:06Z regular-session close (HKEX); Yahoo Finance chart API
inputs.wacc_rationale: Flows are USD and the HKD is pegged to USD, so a USD discount rate: US 10y ~4.3% + beta ~0.9 x 5.5% ERP = ~9.2%, rounded to 9.0% for a debt-free, cash-generative balance sheet (WACC = cost of equity, no debt). Tariff, birth-rate and China-manufacturing risk is carried in the bear scenario and its 25% weight, not as a WACC premium, and the same 9.0% is used in all three scenarios (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. FY2026 lease cash = capital element 23.0 (CF line 6204) + interest on lease liabilities 6.2 (CF line 6196) = US$29.2m = 1.44% of revenue, charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path. D&A path is EX right-of-use depreciation (tangible 31.6 + intangible 0.7 = 32.3, 1.59% of revenue; RoU 22.6 excluded). Lease liabilities (US$126.8m at 31-Mar-2026) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt -- one treatment, not both.
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interests; profit for the year is fully attributable (statement of changes in equity).
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF (component route) with the non-US adaptations (USD flows / HKD quote, IFRS 16 leases treatment B, SBC near-zero). Routed as an operating company: VTech is a debt-free manufacturer/brand owner (ELP toys, residential phones, EMS/CMS) whose value is a free-cash-flow stream; none of the bank/REIT/holdco/distress rows apply, and there is no prior DCF or memory entry, so this is a fresh build. EBITDA basis: adj_ebitda is pre-SBC and pre-lease (IFRS 16) = operating profit 171.0 + D&A 54.9 + SBC 4.1 + associate impairment 2.1 + FV loss 0.2 = US$232.3m (11.46%); FY0 calibration: 232.3 - SBC 4.1 - lease 29.2 - D&A ex-RoU 32.3 = EBIT 166.7, x (1-19.6%) = NOPAT 134.0 vs reported NPAT 134.1 (interest income 2.2 roughly offsets the 2.1 impairment) -- ties. Interest income is excluded from EBITDA (it sits in net finance expense below operating profit) and stripped from last_fcf because net cash (264) > 1x owner FCF. last_fcf = 92.6 - 4.1 - 2.2 = 86.3 by the house definition; deducting the 23.0 lease principal as well (treatment B) gives 63.3, and FY2026 was depressed by a US$79m working-capital build (stocks +42, debtors +19, creditors -19) after tariff-related early builds; FY2024/FY2025 equivalents were ~US$300m / ~US$166m. The forward build does not start from last_fcf -- it builds from components (FY1 owner-FCF ~US$115-120m base). Working capital: stocks 402.9 + debtors 351.8 vs creditors 466.8 + provisions 28.3 = net ~US$260m (~13% of revenue), so wc_capture is -13% (growth consumes cash; a revenue decline releases it). Cash: all US$264m deposits and cash treated as excess; US$18.2m is in PRC banks subject to FX-control rules and the business is H2-weighted (H1 cash troughs ~US$148m), so ~US$18m of the cash is arguably trapped or working cash -- a deliberate simplification worth ~US$0.07 (HK$0.56) per share. Small investments (1.9), associate (1.4) and DB surplus (7.4) omitted (<US$0.05/share). Buybacks: none; the flat count is maintained by the trustee's on-market purchases for the award scheme. SBC-zero-ish market: SBC is 0.2% of revenue so house and street nearly coincide.

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY2027 guidance: group revenue expected to grow, ELP and TEL up, CMS flat; +4% is a partial rebound of the tariff-hit -6.9% FY2026, then fading to 1.5% as birth-rate and landline decline offset CMS growth from Malaysia/Mexico capacity.
base.ebitda_margin_path_rationale: Pre-SBC, pre-IFRS16 EBITDA. FY2026 underlying 11.46%; FY2027 guided gross-margin decline on surging component costs (AI-driven shortages) -> 10.9%; recovering to the FY2022-FY2026 mid-cycle ~11.5% (range 10.7-11.9%; FY2020-21 13-14% was a COVID toy peak).
base.capex_pct_path_rationale: Muar, Malaysia capacity doubling completes mid-2027, lifting FY2027-28 capex above the ~1.5% run-rate.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_rationale: FY2026 ETR 19.6% after BEPS 2.0 global minimum tax; taxation payable rose 15.4 -> 25.8 so cash taxes (25.0) lag the charge and will catch up. Held at 19.5%.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because US tariff policy is a binary, uncontrollable driver that already cut North American ELP 25% in one half, and two of three segments face secular decline (birth rates, landlines). Base 50% because management's FY2027 growth guidance is backed by secured retailer support. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once -- tariff stability, component-cost relief and EMS share wins from the new plants -- and this is not a compounder.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
